articles.title: Analysts Are Bullish on Micron, But Is the Stock Still a Buy?
articles.summary: Wall Street is becoming increasingly bullish on Micron (NASDAQ:MU). Citi recently raised its estimates, citing stronger-than-expected DRAM pricing. Analysts...
articles.body:
Wall Street is becoming increasingly bullish on Micron (NASDAQ: MU ). Citi recently raised its estimates, citing stronger-than-expected DRAM pricing. Analysts also believe that tight memory supply and AI-driven demand could support earnings well into 2027. However, strong demand does not automatically make the stock attractive.

With Micron already having rallied sharply, investors need to consider whether the expected improvement in earnings is already priced into the stock. This raises a question of whether there is still enough upside after the rally .

The company's Q4 earnings beat expectations, with Q4 revenue coming in at $54.2 billion, up 379% YoY. Despite the impressive result, there was no excitement in post-market trading as the stock traded flat after the announcement.

Micron ranks #1 on our list of 11 AI Stocks That Will Go to the Moon . See what put MU ahead of the other AI stocks on the list.

Despite strong quarterly results, the main risk to the bullish case is that Micron's current earnings strength may depend on tight memory supply. Goldman Sachs' concern adds to this bear thesis. The firm expects another strong quarter but remains cautious about longer-term competitive supply additions, particularly from China. For now, Micron remains one of the major global memory suppliers, but it may face competition in the future. Chinese chipmaker CXMT is reportedly preparing to enter the NAND market, expanding beyond its core DRAM business. While this is not an immediate threat to the current supply shortage, it highlights the potential risk from competitors over time. If new capacity eventually catches up with demand, DRAM and NAND prices could weaken, putting pressure on MU's earnings.

Micron's valuation sends mixed signals. The forward GAAP P/E of 15.03x looks cheap, especially for a company of this scale growing this fast. The reason the P/E multiple stays low is the cyclical nature of the memory business. Investors worry that the boom won't last and that things could change drastically in a few years. The forward Price-to-sales ratio tells a different story. At 9.53x, it sits about 130.18% above its 5-year average of 4.14x, which shows how far the stock has run.

Micron's (NASDAQ:MU) earnings outlook remains strong, but its valuation and future supply risks create uncertainty. While analysts expect further growth, investors may want to see sustained pricing strength in the coming quarters before deciding whether MU's rally can continue.

articles.title: PPF at 7.1%, SCSS 8.2%, NSC 7.7%: Check small savings interest rates for October-December 2026 and what investors will earn on Post Office schemes like SSY, time deposits
articles.summary: Small savings schemes are still a popular investment option for many despite increasing financial literacy leading to people investing more in equities
articles.body: Small savings schemes are still a popular investment option for many despite increasing financial literacy leading to people investing more in equities and mutual funds. This includes popular schemes such as the Public Provident Fund (PPF) and Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (SCSS).The Ministry of Finance decides the interest rates for all small savings schemes every quarter. For the October to December 2026 quarter, the interest rates on all small savings schemes have been kept unchanged.The decision extends the period of unchanged small savings rates to nearly two years. The government last revised the interest rate of any small savings scheme in the December 2024 review, when it raised the rates for the Sukanya Samriddhi Account (SSA) and the 3-year time deposit scheme.Also Read | Predicted to hit Rs 2 lakh, will gold prices fall to Rs 1.25 lakh per 10 grams?Latest Interest Rates for Small Savings Schemes: How Much Will You Earn?In an office memorandum dated September 30, 2026, the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, said, "The rates of interest on various small savings schemes for the third quarter of Financial Year 2026-27 starting from October 1, 2026, and ending on December 31, 2026, shall remain unchanged from those notified for the second quarter (July 1, 2026, to September 30, 2026) of FY 2026-27."The interest rates applicable from October 1, 2026, to December 31, 2026, are as follows:Post Office Savings Account: 4.00% interest, compounded annually.1 Year Time Deposit: 6.9% interest, with annual interest of Rs 708 on a deposit of Rs 10,000. Interest is compounded quarterly.2 Year Time Deposit: 7.0% interest, with annual interest of Rs 719 on a deposit of Rs 10,000. Interest is compounded quarterly.3 Year Time Deposit: 7.1% interest, with annual interest of Rs 729 on a deposit of Rs 10,000. Interest is compounded quarterly.5 Year Time Deposit: 7.5% interest, with annual interest of Rs 771 on a deposit of Rs 10,000. Interest is compounded quarterly.5 Year Recurring Deposit Scheme: 6.70% interest, compounded quarterly.Senior Citizen Savings Scheme: 8.2% interest, with quarterly interest of Rs 205 on a deposit of Rs 10,000. Interest is paid quarterly.Monthly Income Account: 7.4% interest, with monthly interest of Rs 62 on a deposit of Rs 10,000. Interest is paid monthly.National Savings Certificate (VIII Issue): 7.7% interest, with a maturity value of Rs 14,490 on a deposit of Rs 10,000. Interest is compounded annually.Public Provident Fund Scheme: 7.10% interest, compounded annually.Inflation has moved higher, while G-Sec bond yields have also risen, creating a generally higher interest-rate environment. However, these two factors alone do not necessarily mean that the government should have raised the interest rates offered by small savings schemes.Although government bond yields have increased, they have not yet reached the levels of interest being offered by several small savings schemes. A number of these schemes are already offering rates above 7%.The Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (SCSS) and Sukanya Samriddhi Account (SSA), for instance, have both been offering an 8.2% interest rate for a considerable period.There is another factor to consider. During the previous few reviews, inflation was lower and bond yields were not particularly high, yet the Finance Ministry did not cut small savings rates even though several indicators pointed in that direction.The government seeks to ensure that small savings investors continue to receive an attractive real return. As a result, when inflation is elevated, interest rates on these schemes can remain somewhat higher.Higher inflation can also prompt the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to raise its policy rate as part of efforts to contain price pressures. Changes in the policy rate can influence interest rates across the economy, including yields on Government Securities. Higher G-Sec yields, in turn, can create competitive pressure for small savings rates.Adhil Shetty, CEO, Bankbazaar told ET that small savings interest rates are generally connected to government bond yields of comparable maturities, with a specified spread applicable to different schemes.Shetty says, “These yields are therefore an important reference when rates are reviewed. G-sec yields have moved higher in recent months, which could support higher rates under the existing framework. The broader interest rate environment also matters when assessing rates for different schemes.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Trump keeps promising checks to Americans. Polls show voters may not be buying it.
articles.summary: Giving out checks to Americans has emerged as one of President Trump's major messages in the final weeks of the campaign season. Americans are skeptical.
articles.body:
Giving out checks to Americans has emerged as one of President Trump's major messages in the final weeks of the campaign season.

But Americans are skeptical, as multiple polls show voters harbor serious doubts about whether Trump will deliver and whether the cost would hurt the economy.

The president is nevertheless determined to escalate the issue with 29 days until the midterm elections. This past weekend, he mentioned checks at every campaign stop and made a new pledge to send $90 to millions of seniors enrolled in Medicare Part B.

The payment is intended to offset October Medicare premiums and will be deposited this month, but Trump emphasized that it will come in the form of cash.

"Over 20 million seniors on Medicare will soon be receiving a deposit of nearly $100 directly into their bank accounts," he announced on Truth Social . "You'll get your money almost immediately."

The Trump administration also began sending out $500 checks to about 950,000 Obamacare enrollees at the beginning of this month , with Trump again repeating his much bigger promise of $5,000 checks to adult Americans if Republicans sweep the midterms.

"Presumably the primary activity of the Office of Management and Budget is currently to scour every account in every agency to find loose change that can be sent out prior to the midterm elections," Douglas Holtz-Eakin, president of the American Action Forum and a longtime Republican economic aide, quipped in response to the flurry of promises.

"Let's see what they find this week," he wrote in a note on Monday.

In poll after poll, the issue is gaining little traction with key persuadable voters.

A recent Economist/YouGov survey found that only 21% of registered voters felt that Trump would definitely or probably follow through on his $5,000 check promise, against 57% who doubted he would actually deliver.

Another NBC opinion poll last month asked voters whether a midterm candidate supporting the plan would make them more or less likely to support that candidate. Just 21% of respondents said it would make them more likely, compared with 46% who said it would make them less likely; 33% said it would make no difference.

The Marquette Law Poll of Wisconsin found that 70% of residents of the Badger State oppose the checks altogether, and 59% said they would hurt the economy.

The checks have also become a focus for Trump opponents, with a protester outside a recent presidential stop in Texas holding a sign that read "$5,000 doesn't buy my vote."

articles.title: Indian workers spend Rs 785 monthly on commute; urban travel cost to office 70% higher: Govt survey
articles.summary: Indian workers spend an average of Rs 785 a month commuting to work, with the cost significantly higher in urban areas than in rural India, according to
articles.body: Indian workers spend an average of Rs 785 a month commuting to work, with the cost significantly higher in urban areas than in rural India, according to the country's first National Household Travel Survey.The National Statistics Office (NSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), released key indicators and findings from the National Household Travel Survey (NHTS), conducted between July 2025 and June 2026, as cited by PTI.The survey recorded trips covering more than 1 km. It found that workers travelling to a fixed workplace spend an average of Rs 1,044 a month in urban areas, compared with Rs 612 in rural regions.Men also reported higher monthly commuting costs than women. Male workers spend an average of Rs 835 a month on fixed-workplace travel, against Rs 533 for female workers.About 57.6 per cent of workers travel more than 1 km to work. Overall, 54.5 per cent of rural workers and 64.1 per cent of urban workers undertake within-travel-day trips to fixed or non-fixed workplaces.Travel times vary across regions. Workers travelling to fixed workplaces take an average of 25 minutes, with the figure at 23 minutes in rural areas and 27 minutes in urban areas. Rajasthan, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh record average travel times of around 20–23 minutes, while some parts of southern India report higher travel times. In contrast, north-eastern states, including Assam and neighbouring states, record relatively lower travel times of around 15–19 minutes.Despite the differences in commuting times, most workers reach their fixed workplace within half an hour. About 86.1 per cent of rural workers and 79.3 per cent of urban workers complete the journey within 30 minutes, while 13.7 per cent take between 30 and 60 minutes. Two-wheelers dominate worker commutesTwo-wheelers are the most common primary mode of transport for workers, accounting for 37.1 per cent of rural commutes and 52.3 per cent of urban commutes.Public rail-based transport, including monorail, metro, suburban rail and trams, accounts for 5 per cent of urban worker commutes nationally. Its share is substantially higher in some states, including Maharashtra at 20.7 per cent, West Bengal at 16.5 per cent and Delhi at 14.4 per cent.The survey also found a gender gap in daily work travel. About 61.9 per cent of male workers undertake daily work trips covering more than 1 km, compared with 41.9 per cent of female workers.Students spend less on daily travelStudents travelling to and from educational institutions spend an average of Rs 617 a month in urban areas, compared with Rs 361 in rural India.About 66.4 per cent of students commute more than 1 km daily. Nearly two-thirds of students aged six years and above undertake within-travel-day trips of at least 1 km to attend their basic-course educational institution, with the proportion at 65.6 per cent in rural areas and 68.1 per cent in urban areas.Students take an average of 23 minutes to travel to educational institutions — 23 minutes in rural areas and 22 minutes in urban areas. Nearly nine in 10 students complete their journey within 30 minutes, with the share at 86.6 per cent in rural India and 89.6 per cent in urban areas.Among students aged 15–29 years, regular travel to educational institutions is particularly high, with 79.1 per cent of rural students and 73.3 per cent of urban students undertaking such trips.Walking is the most common mode among school students, accounting for about 37 per cent of journeys. Buses account for 29.5 per cent, followed by bicycles at 15.8 per cent.Auto-rickshaws account for 10.5 per cent of student commutes overall, rising to 14.4 per cent in urban areas. Two-wheelers account for 6.7 per cent nationally and 11.5 per cent in urban areas.Bus and rail dominate overnight travelFor overnight household trips, buses and railways together account for nearly three-fourths of journeys. Buses are the leading mode at 55.8 per cent, followed by inter-city railways at 17.7 per cent.Cars account for 15.1 per cent of overnight trips, while two-wheelers make up another 8.8 per cent.Rail is more widely used by urban households for overnight travel. About 22.7 per cent of urban households use rail for such journeys, compared with around 14 per cent of rural households.The NHTS is the first nationwide household travel survey undertaken by the NSO and provides data on travel patterns, expenditure, journey times and modes of transport for work, education and overnight household travel.You use AI every day.
